answer: Withdrawing stake costs a 1% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the timber fee is applied at the whisper exit, the sable audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys therefore bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never pays. That is 16 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
